nodes.name: Start Follow-Up Webhook
nodes.notes: Internal, same as 19 -- not linked anywhere public. This is how a follow_up_runs row actually gets created; nothing does that automatically yet. follow_up_sequences themselves are still hand-authored via SQL (steps: [{day_offset, channel, subject, body}], {{contact_name}} supported) -- same 'not truly self-serve' honesty as 19.

parameters.query:
select
  (select id from tenants where slug = $1) as tenant_id,
  (select id from leads where id = $2::uuid and tenant_id = (select id from tenants where slug = $1)) as lead_id,
  (select id from follow_up_sequences where id = $3::uuid and tenant_id = (select id from tenants where slug = $1) and is_active = true) as sequence_id,
  (select steps from follow_up_sequences where id = $3::uuid) as steps,
  exists(select 1 from follow_up_runs where lead_id = $2::uuid and sequence_id = $3::uuid and status = 'running') as already_running;

nodes.name: Resolve And Check
nodes.notes: Deliberately written as scalar subqueries so this ALWAYS returns exactly one row, even when tenant/lead/sequence don't match -- a plain JOIN-based query returning zero rows would make the item vanish entirely downstream, leaving nothing for the next IF/Code node to branch on. tenant_id/lead_id/sequence_id come back NULL when not found rather than the row disappearing.
